utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, this is not an assumption. This is an elementary fact which an educated officer must know about. A person who is replacing a commander and is his deputy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, the Brinja feature and trig 450, is that east of all these places that your deputy recorded in the additions to the diary?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely that. Easterly and south-easterly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you, to all intents and purposes -- or, rather, did you pass by all those places?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Milosevic, if I said that the axis of action, although -- the axis my unit moved was from west to east and I was more easterly than the villages enumerated, then it is quite normal that I had to pass through those villages. And everybody who can read and write must realise that. It must be clear to one and all, let alone an officer, which is what my deputy was. He was an excellent officer, to boot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, here it says, "I have decided," and then it says "Bela Crkva, Celine, Nogavac, Velika Hoca," and then I place a line there because after Velika Hoca, there's Brinja and trig 450. Velika Krusa I meant to say. Not Velika Hoca, Velika Krusa.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said Bela Crkva-Celine-Nogavac is one axis and the other axis is Velika Hoca-Mala Hoca, which is located more westerly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No, I made the mistake. I made the mistake.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The axis is quite clear: It's the general axis of the action, and I said that automatically from this document it was copied out. The villages we passed through were copied out. Since I didn't inform him of any of the consequences, there was no need for him to enter anything else, nor did he have the possibility of checking this out in another way; where we were, what village we were in, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. We've clarified that point. Now, let's clarify the first three words he used. He said, "Surrounded and cleaned," and then he mentioned the villages you passed through. Read the first page of the order by the commander. What does it say? Order --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find that. May I take a moment to find this? I've lost my way in all this paperwork and documents. Just a moment, please. I seem to have mislaid that first page somewhere. Could you help me out here, please, and give me that first page, because I've mislaid it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will. It is tab 3, and I'll give you the page.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had to deal with such a lot of documents on one place, so I'm not finding my way very well. But it's there somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We'll hand it over to you in a moment.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you find it when you're not looking for it. Yes. It was right here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back to the question. I want you to explain the first three words at the beginning of this. We've explained the geographic points. Now it says, "Blocked and cleaned." That's what he wrote. What does it say in the actual order by the brigade commander? The title, the heading.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Order on destroying Siptar terrorist forces in the broader area of the village of Retimlje, lifting the blockade of the communication line Suva Reka-Orahovac, and establishing control of the territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, what is defined in the order where all these places are located in the decision on page 2, he wrote down that they had been blocked and cleaned. That's the entry he made. So what activity is it? What does the order say? The order is for?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Destroying Siptar terrorist forces in the general sector of the village of Retimlje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that blocked and cleaned, that phrase "blocked and cleaned," can that be explained in any other way than to refer to Siptar terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that long time ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic. Mr. Milosevic, you very well know that is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, more than that: We're seeing the waste of that most precious resource in this case, which is the time allocated to the accused to bring his Defence, and he's the person who is wasting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said your deputy had this order.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. It was the only copy we had at the command post in Zub village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So what did he imply under "blocked and cleaned"?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing that I implied when I explained the term. It means the area was blocked and cleaned from armed terrorists. But I would also like to draw your attention to the third page, to paragraph 5.5, which also gives a specific task for the battalion. And I explained why my unit did not carry out a search of Bela Crkva village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just wait. This needs to be clear for everyone. In paragraph 5.5, it says task for --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combat Group 2. And then it says: "Carry out an energetic attack to search the village of Bela Crkva, emerge on the Brnjaca line, Brod elevation, trig point 432, trig point 440," and so on and so forth, "In coordinated action ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it says: "In a coordinated action cut off and destroy terrorist Siptar forces in the village of Celine," and et cetera, "seal off Velika Krusa."

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, that's what it says. I said already that I had relevant information to the effect that there were no terrorists in Bela Crkva, and that's why we didn't search it. And anyway, the brigade commander passed along the fringes of Bela Crkva that very morning, along the asphalt road that leads from to Zrze towards Orahovac because he was on his way to his command post. And he even sent from Brnjaca elevation a part of my unit towards Amovac because the man knew this area very well. He is a native of Kosovo and Metohija and lived there for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Here in the task that your deputy had in his hands at the command post, it says: "Carry out an energetic attack to search the village of Bela Crkva."

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he thought that that part of the task had been carried out, logically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Whereas you explained why there was no energetic attack, because --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was no terrorist activity. And throughout 1998 and 1999 in Kosovo and Metohija, the practice was the same: Wherever there was no terrorist activity, there was no action on our part because it would not make sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, you've now lost me completely. Why should he assume blocked and cleaned from the word "search the village," when in relation to other villages the words "destroy STS" is specifically used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, you would have to read the entire text of the task. And from the entire text of the task you could understand what the answer is to this question. Because the point of searching terrain -- the purpose of searching terrain is precisely to detect terrorists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But, Mr. Vukovic, how can you assume that terrorists will be found? Search presupposes that either you may or may not find terrorists in that particular location. Your deputy seems to have assumed, according to you, that terrorists were found, because he used the word "cleaned."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I've already said he just automatically copied from the task that was in the document in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If he did that, that raises the much wider question of whether all the analyses that are placed before us are ultimately just copies of what the original plan was. I mean, I'm simply explaining to you that I, first of all, don't understand the explanation and, secondly, insofar as I can make some sense of it, it doesn't seem to me to be helpful to the case that's being presented.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can repeat from the beginning, if you allow me. The analysis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're failing to explain to me at all why the deputy would use the word "cleaned" when all that was ordered was a search.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the purpose of a search is precisely to establish whether there are terrorists in a certain area, and if there are, to eliminate them from that era. That is the purpose of the entire action. And an action is executed by blocking and searching a certain area or location. I don't know of any different way to explain this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: For the sake of a comprehensive explanation, read the previous paragraph, 4. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In coordinated action --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Skip that. Say what follows in the first line.

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. "Lift the blockade off the Suva Reka-Orahovac road. Cut off and destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the general sector of the village of Retimlje."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Does it go on to mention Bela Crkva, Nogavac, Velika Hoca, and so on?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was the general axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does the order of the brigade commander say cut off and destroy?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that's what your deputy saw, block and destroy?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "Block and destroy Siptar terrorist forces." That's what is written?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So we have that --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What his words refer to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Show me where that is in relation to Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the same paragraph that is item 4, which begins, "I have decided ..." And then in line number 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not seeing it. Oh, yes, I have number 4 now. I can see "I have decided ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says: "Block and destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the broader area of Retimlje village and establish control of the territory in this area." Block and destroy. How? By grouping the main forces on the said axes, naming both. One is Bela Crkva-Celine-Nogavac, and the other one is Velika Hoca-Mala Hoca and so on. So if you disregard what is not relevant to this question, it says: "Block and destroy on the axes Bela Crkva-Nogavac, Velika Hoca-Mala Hoca, the Siptar terrorist forces." It's all in one paragraph here. Block and destroy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nort, could you turn over to the other page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, this is paragraph 4 where he communicates the purpose of that activity, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nort, just go back to the previous page. Yes. Thanks. That's enough, just go back now to the other page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, paragraph 5 has this heading "Unit assignments." Wherein the brigade commander within this mission called blocking and is destruction of Siptar terrorist forces determines the activities for each unit, what they are supposed to do. So within the general task of blocking and destroying Siptar terrorist forces in point 5.5, it says: "Carry out an energetic attack to search the village of Bela Crkva, to emerge on the Brnjaca line ..." et cetera, et cetera. So this is a reference to an energetic attack whereas Colonel Vukovic explained this would have happened, indeed, if there had been any terrorists in Bela Crkva. Since there weren't any, they just passed through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there were terrorists in the following villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, when he quoted from this passage of the 30th of March where you say that around 2.000 people have passed by or crossed --

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it with me. Could you give me a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: To save time, I'll read it. I hope nobody will think that I will intentionally misread. You say that around 2.000 people had passed, whereupon Mr. Nice said you recorded that as a satisfactory result. Please tell me, do you enter into your war diary satisfactory or unsatisfactory results or do you enter facts?

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I record facts. As far as satisfaction is concerned, if you think that it is satisfactory to record your own losses, then so be it. As for the Siptar civilian movements, I also recorded what I felt about that. Nobody can watch other people suffering while remaining indifferent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In fact, you wrote in your diary: "There is nothing sadder than to watch a couple of poor people who are leaving their homes on somebody's instruction."

utterances.speaker: VLATKO VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wrote and that's what I continue to think to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... in chief and in cross-examination. We are simply spending time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, Mr. Nice particularly insisted on Bela Crkva and almost proclaimed that Colonel Vukovic had admitted to ethnic cleansing based on his entries in the diary. His entries in the diary are very clear because you have the order, which is a strict one, and you have his testimony. Plus you have the map where you can see where exactly he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic. Your position, Mr. Milosevic, on the word "ciscenje" is that whenever it is used it is used in relation to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. And I don't know of any officer - you can bring any number of VJ officers - who can tell you any different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer do you have in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not much, I hope. I believe if you give me a slight extension I can finish now, not to detain the witness further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is a case here this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I also have time problems as well. I'm not available. I've got to leave very promptly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. We have to adjourn, and you'll have to return, Colonel, next week, Wednesday, the 9th of November, at 9.00 a.m. We will adjourn until that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of November, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
